english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^{2}e^{-4x}$, and let $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $g(x)=f^{(9)}(x)$, where $f^{(9)}$ denotes the ninth derivative of $f$. Then the sum of the $x$-coordinates of all the points of inflection of the graph of $y=g(x)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^{2}e^{-4x}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, तथा $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=f^{(9)}(x)$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, जहाँ $f^{(9)}$, $f$ का नौवाँ अवकलज है। तब $y=g(x)$ के आलेख के सभी नति परिवर्तन बिन्दुओं के $x$-निर्देशांकों का योग ______ है।
solution: Leibniz rule (only three terms survive since $(x^{2})'''=0$): $f^{(n)}(x)=(-4)^{n-2}e^{-4x}\left[16x^{2}-8nx+n(n-1)\right]$
Points of inflection of $g=f^{(9)}$: where $g''=f^{(11)}$ changes sign
$f^{(11)}(x)=(-4)^{9}e^{-4x}\left[16x^{2}-88x+110\right]$; $e^{-4x}>0$, so the sign is that of the quadratic
Discriminant $=88^{2}-64\cdot110=704>0$: two simple roots, and $g''$ changes sign at each, so both are points of inflection
solution_full: By the Leibniz rule, $f^{(n)}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}\left(x^{2}\right)^{(k)}\left(e^{-4x}\right)^{(n-k)}$. Only $k=0,1,2$ contribute because $\left(x^{2}\right)^{(k)}=0$ for $k\ge3$, and $\left(e^{-4x}\right)^{(m)}=(-4)^{m}e^{-4x}$.
$g=f^{(9)}$ is twice differentiable and $g''=f^{(11)}$. A point of inflection of $y=g(x)$ is where $g''$ changes sign.
With $n=11$: $g''(x)=(-4)^{9}e^{-4x}\left[16x^{2}-88x+110\right]$. Since $e^{-4x}>0$ and $(-4)^{9}$ is a non-zero constant, the sign of $g''$ changes exactly where $16x^{2}-88x+110$ changes sign.

Its discriminant is $88^{2}-4\cdot16\cdot110=7744-7040=704>0$, so it has two distinct real roots $x=\dfrac{11\pm\sqrt{11}}{4}$. At each simple root the quadratic changes sign, so $g$ has exactly two points of inflection.
By Vieta, the sum of their $x$-coordinates is $\dfrac{88}{16}=\dfrac{11}{2}=5.50$.
originality_note: New: the points of inflection of a high-order derivative g = f^(9), found from the closed form of the n-th derivative by Leibniz's rule and read off by Vieta (way 5). Closest known: n-th derivative of x^2 e^{ax} by Leibniz; inflection points of x^n e^{-x}. Different because: the curve examined is the ninth derivative itself, so the student must go two orders further (f^(11)) and confirm the sign change at simple roots.

concept_use.Higher order derivatives: f^(9) and f^(11) come from the Leibniz formula for the n-th derivative of x^2 e^{-4x}.
concept_use.Concavity, Convexity & Points of Inflect: Points of inflection of g are where g'' = f^(11) changes sign; both simple roots of 16x^2 - 88x + 110 qualify.
